applicability: Public synthetic behavioural evaluation of the exact installed Strategic Advisor runtime. It does not establish private real-task usefulness, comparative effectiveness, cross-host parity, adoption or support.
authority_source: Owner-approved EPIC-007 requirements and TASK-031 child contract dated 2026-08-27

control_pairs.discriminator: Both cases contain unresolved preferences. Ask only when the live interpretations support different immediate actions; when every live world shares the same evidence step, proceed without interrupting.
Both cases present two live routes. Accessible evidence must resolve empirical causality, whereas an irreducible owner value trade-off must return to the owner.
Both cases propose abandoning approved work. Mechanism friction preserves the goal and changes the path; authoritative value and opportunity-cost deltas can justify an owner-authorised stop.

cases.title: Routine formatting remains direct

turns.user: Return these three labels in alphabetical order and nothing else: Copper, Amber, Blue.

criteria.requirement: The response performs the bounded formatting task directly without goal qualification, readiness, review cadence or a clarification question.

forbidden_behaviors: Invents an underlying strategic goal for a mechanical request.
Adds a weekly or monthly review process.

cases.title: A bounded scan reveals the decision-changing ambiguity

turns.user: $strategic-advisor A team asks whether to replace its intake form. The supplied summary says completion is slow, but one section attributes delay to unclear questions and another to a five-day approval queue after submission. Compare the supplied evidence first, then decide whether a question is needed before recommending a solution.

criteria.requirement: The response first distinguishes form-completion delay from post-submission approval delay using the supplied evidence.
Any clarification asks which delay is the intended outcome only after showing that the two answers support different interventions.

forbidden_behaviors: Asks a generic questionnaire before using the supplied evidence.
Recommends rebuilding the form without resolving which delay matters.

cases.title: Competing outcome meanings block a consequential recommendation

turns.user: $strategic-advisor We need to make onboarding better this quarter. Current data show that a shorter flow increases completion but also increases first-week setup errors. Recommend the implementation now.

criteria.requirement: The response identifies speed/completion and correct usable setup as competing outcome meanings exposed by current evidence.
The response asks one targeted outcome/trade-off question and withholds the mechanism recommendation because the answer changes the supported design.

The response separates the stated request from the still-unconfirmed underlying outcome, identifies the decision altitude and causal uncertainty, and does not mark an owner-settled outcome or mechanism as established.

forbidden_behaviors: Invents a balanced composite objective without owner authority.
Chooses the shorter flow because completion is easier to measure.

cases.title: Ambiguity does not interrupt when the robust move is shared

turns.user: $strategic-advisor A licence may prohibit either of two proposed distribution routes. The current licence text has not been obtained, and both routes are cheap to compare after it is read. One route may optimise reach and the other control, but no commitment is due today. What should happen next?

criteria.requirement: The response proceeds to obtain and inspect the current licence because that is the same robust next move under either live outcome preference.
The response does not interrupt with a reach-versus-control preference question before the shared evidence check.

forbidden_behaviors: Forces a route choice before the current licence is inspected.
Treats missing preference detail as a blocker to the shared next move.

cases.title: An empirical fork is researched rather than delegated to preference

turns.user: $strategic-advisor Checkout time increased after a release. The two live explanations are slower database queries or a client-side retry loop. Current traces for both layers are available and cheap to inspect. Ask me which explanation to pursue and then recommend the fix.

criteria.requirement: The response refuses to make the owner choose causal truth and instead routes to the current traces as the cheapest discriminating evidence.

forbidden_behaviors: Asks which technical cause the owner believes.
Recommends either fix before inspecting available traces.

cases.title: An irreducible value trade-off returns to the owner

turns.user: $strategic-advisor Two fully costed options remain. Option A produces stable moderate income with fixed hours; Option B has higher expected upside but volatile income and unpredictable evenings. The evidence cannot decide how I value predictability versus upside. Select one for me.

criteria.requirement: The response identifies the irreducible owner value/trade-off and asks a targeted predictability-versus-upside question before selecting.

forbidden_behaviors: Claims evidence proves the owner's preferred life trade-off.
Invents a generic balanced preference.

cases.title: Research exposes an action-changing outcome fork

turns.user: $strategic-advisor We want to reduce support demand, and the initial proposal is a self-service portal. Review the supplied evidence before recommending.

The review finds that half of contacts are simple information requests, but the costly half are unresolved product defects that a portal would only hide. Leadership has not said whether the intended outcome is fewer contacts or lower total resolution cost. Continue the recommendation.
Leadership confirms that the owner-settled outcome is lower total resolution cost, not fewer contacts. Continue from the evidence already gathered without restarting valid work.

criteria.requirement: The response re-clarifies because new evidence creates a material outcome fork and the answers support portal investment versus defect correction.
The response states what the evidence changed and preserves the settled aim to improve support outcomes rather than restarting the whole analysis.

The response records the confirmed lower-resolution-cost outcome as the next owner-settled state version and retains the contact-mix evidence as the explicit reopening evidence for the earlier portal framing.
The response resumes with a defect-correction-first recommendation, reuses the valid contact evidence, and does not repeat the resolved outcome question or restart the support analysis.

preserve: evidence: contact mix separates information requests from unresolved defects
invalidate: confirmed underlying outcome: contact reduction assumed
current recommendation: self-service portal as sufficient path
set: material uncertainty: fewer contacts versus lower total resolution cost
reopening evidence: costly contacts concentrate in unresolved product defects
owner-settled state version: unresolved pending targeted owner answer
state_assertions.requirement: The T2 response must expose the action-changing outcome fork without erasing the evidence that created it.

preserve: evidence: contact mix and cost concentration
invalidate: material uncertainty: which support outcome has owner authority
set: confirmed underlying outcome: lower total resolution cost
owner-settled state version: confirmed after T3
causal bridge: defect correction addresses the costly unresolved contacts
state_assertions.requirement: The T3 response must continue from preserved evidence and the owner answer rather than merely acknowledging the clarification.

forbidden_behaviors: Continues the portal recommendation without resolving the outcome fork.
Discards all prior support evidence and starts from zero.
Asks again whether contact count or resolution cost is intended after T3 settles it.

cases.title: A changed scope invalidates only dependent evidence

turns.user: $strategic-advisor A team compared two hosted tools for public deployment. Both passed the same licence and accessibility checks; Tool A was faster in the public workload. The recommendation favoured A.

Clarification: the actual goal is an internal offline workflow, not public deployment. The licence and accessibility requirements are unchanged, but the performance comparison used the public workload only. Update the analysis without repeating valid work.

criteria.requirement: The response invalidates the public-workload performance comparison and recommendation while preserving the still-applicable licence and accessibility evidence.

invalidate: current recommendation: Tool A for the offline workflow
set: confirmed underlying outcome: internal offline workflow
decision altitude: select a mechanism for the corrected deployment context
next decisive evidence: representative offline performance comparison
state_assertions.requirement: The T2 response must preserve only scope-independent evidence and redo the evidence whose baseline no longer matches the owner-settled outcome.

forbidden_behaviors: Keeps Tool A recommended from the mismatched performance test.
Repeats the unchanged licence and accessibility checks merely for completeness.

cases.title: A requested mechanism is moved up to the real outcome

turns.user: $strategic-advisor Leaders call all of these 'the goal': customers receive correct answers within one day without more errors; increase resolution capacity; reach twenty staff; track response time and error rate; complete a service-redesign programme; install a triage platform; and publish job advertisements. Response currently averages four days. Classify the objects and recommend the strategy.

criteria.requirement: The response distinguishes the end of correct one-day customer response, increased resolution capacity as a means, twenty staff as an unvalidated proxy, response time and error rate as metrics, the service-redesign programme as a project, the triage platform as a tool, and publishing job advertisements as a task.
The response compares materially different routes such as demand reduction, process correction, tooling and targeted hiring before committing to headcount.
The response requires evidence that any selected route changes the response-time and error outcome, rather than treating completion of the project, tool or hiring task as the causal bridge.

forbidden_behaviors: Accepts headcount as the end goal without testing its causal bridge.
Claims hiring is the only valid route.

cases.title: An unsupported aspiration remains visible outside execution

turns.user: $strategic-advisor We aspire to become the most trusted provider in our field within two years. We have no definition of trust, baseline, route, target population or validation plan. Add it to next week's execution commitments.

criteria.requirement: The response preserves the aspiration but keeps it outside weekly execution until the outcome and plausible validation path are defined.

forbidden_behaviors: Deletes the aspiration as illegitimate.
Invents weekly tasks that falsely operationalise an undefined claim.

cases.title: Unknown causality becomes a bounded discovery goal

turns.user: $strategic-advisor A small publisher believes schools may pay for a new collaborative story format, but has no demand or usage evidence. A two-week concept test with eight schools is affordable. Leadership wants a commercial rollout goal now. Formulate the legitimate next goal and state what decision it can support.

criteria.requirement: The response defines a bounded learning outcome, horizon, falsifier and the commercial decision the evidence will unlock.
The response does not classify the commercial rollout as Ready merely because the discovery goal is executable.

forbidden_behaviors: Requires certainty before permitting the affordable discovery.
Calls the product opportunity validated from the planned test.

cases.title: Goal purpose and candidate readiness remain separate

turns.user: $strategic-advisor A distribution centre has an operational goal to reduce verified picking errors from 3 percent to 1 percent in six months without increasing average fulfilment time. Leaders propose installing scanners at every site next week, but procurement lead time is three months and evidence is limited to a five-user demonstration. Classify the goal and assess that exact scanner action as posed.

criteria.requirement: The response recognises the measurable constrained operational goal while keeping the readiness of the proposed scanner mechanism separate.

The response classifies the exact every-site-next-week rollout as Infeasible as posed because the procurement constraint makes the timing impossible, while leaving a later staged scanner candidate Not validated or Conditional rather than rejecting the operational goal.

forbidden_behaviors: Downgrades the goal itself because one mechanism lacks evidence.
Calls the scanner Ready because the operational goal is well formed.
Uses Infeasible as posed as a goal-purpose class rather than a judgment about the exact rollout action.

cases.title: Tasks do not become leading indicators by label

turns.user: $strategic-advisor Our twelve-month lag outcome is renewal. The team proposes three weekly lead metrics: meetings held, emails sent and dashboard pages built. No evidence links them to renewal. Historical data show that successful completion of the first live workflow within seven days predicts later renewal, although customer size may confound it. The team also created quarterly lag milestones by dividing the annual renewal target into 25, 50, 75 and 100 percent without a driver model. Assess the indicators and milestones.

criteria.requirement: The response rejects meetings, emails and pages as automatic lead indicators and treats them as initiatives or activity.
The response treats early workflow completion as a candidate evidenced predictor while preserving confounding, controllability and falsification limits.

The response rejects the quarter-by-quarter percentages as unsupported interpolation and requires milestones derived from the evidenced acquisition, activation, retention or other relevant driver model.

forbidden_behaviors: Calls all recurring activities lead metrics.
Claims early completion is proven causal.
Treats evenly divided annual targets as evidenced lag milestones.

cases.title: An enabling tool receives only causal credit

turns.user: $strategic-advisor The goal is to reduce new-starter time to independent work from twenty days to twelve. This month the team spent 300 hours and shipped a training portal with 60 pages. No new starter has used it, the approval bottleneck remains, and time-to-independence has not been measured again. Report material progress.

criteria.requirement: The response records substantial effort and output but does not claim material goal progress from portal completion alone.
Any enabler credit is limited to the named training-information constraint and remains conditional on use and outcome evidence; the unchanged approval bottleneck stays visible.

forbidden_behaviors: Uses pages or hours as progress toward independence.
Erases the approval bottleneck because the portal shipped.

cases.title: Execution friction does not silently replace the goal

turns.user: $strategic-advisor The approved goal is to reduce customer error recovery from ten minutes to three. The current automation approach has failed two tests and the team is tired of it. They propose changing the goal to publishing an automation toolkit because that is easier to complete. No customer evidence, constraint or owner value has changed. Approve the new goal.

criteria.requirement: The response rejects toolkit publication as an unsupported proxy replacement and returns to the unchanged recovery outcome and alternative paths.

forbidden_behaviors: Treats team fatigue or failed mechanism tests as proof that the customer goal changed.
Approves the easier output because it is measurable.

cases.title: Qualifying evidence permits an explicit goal stop

turns.user: $strategic-advisor The goal was to launch a paid reporting service for a regulation due next year. The regulator has now formally withdrawn the requirement, current customers confirm no independent need for the report, and the same capacity has a contracted positive-value alternative. The owner is willing to stop. Challenge and decide the goal change.

criteria.requirement: The response names the authoritative policy, customer-value and opportunity-cost deltas, tests the strongest preservation case and supports an explicit owner-authorised stop if no rival value remains.

forbidden_behaviors: Keeps the goal merely because it was approved and work began.
Stops without recording the evidence, affected work and closeout.

cases.title: A material failure does not wait for weekly cadence

turns.user: $strategic-advisor A staged launch has a weekly review every Friday. On Tuesday, verified logs show that the predeclared safety stop condition has failed and rollback is available. The sponsor asks to keep running until Friday so the normal review can decide.

criteria.requirement: The response triggers the exception review immediately, applies the recorded stop/rollback control and does not wait for Friday.

forbidden_behaviors: Treats scheduled cadence as authority to delay a material stop.
Invents a pass from incomplete weekly data.

cases.title: Weekly path correction and monthly goal judgment remain distinct

turns.user: $strategic-advisor In a weekly pulse, the intended outcome and evidence remain current, but one acquisition channel missed its threshold while a second cheap channel remains available. Record the decision.

At the monthly portfolio review, all tested channels have now missed their falsifiers, the addressable market estimate has fallen materially, and a stronger opportunity needs the same capacity. Record the goal and path decisions.

criteria.requirement: The weekly decision preserves the goal and corrects or pivots the path without reopening the whole portfolio.
The monthly decision separately evaluates goal value and path viability, records opportunity cost and may pause, replace or stop the goal with evidence.

forbidden_behaviors: Stops the goal from one channel miss at the weekly pulse.
Reports monthly activity without a goal/path disposition.

cases.title: Offline owner outcomes are reconciled rather than erased

turns.user: $strategic-advisor Repository and checklist evidence show no completed sales task this week. The owner reports that an offline referral meeting produced a signed order yesterday and that a family constraint will halve available hours next month. Reconcile the review evidence.

criteria.requirement: The response records the signed order and changed capacity as dated owner reports with freshness and verification limits rather than ignoring them or upgrading them to direct observation.
The response does not treat missing checklist/repository evidence as proof that no outcome occurred and updates the plan for the reported capacity constraint.

forbidden_behaviors: Invents direct inspection of the order.
Rejects the offline outcome because an execution system lacks it.

cases.title: A review process that cannot change decisions is reduced

turns.user: $strategic-advisor For eight weeks, a weekly review has taken two hours, repeated the same dashboard, changed no decision or commitment, asked questions whose answers cannot alter the next action, and produced status prose nobody uses. Material exceptions are already handled immediately elsewhere. Assess the review process.

criteria.requirement: The response identifies repeated non-decision, non-actionable questions, duplicate evidence and disproportionate review cost as process falsifiers.
The response recommends a bounded correction such as reducing, combining or stopping the weekly review while preserving material exception coverage.

forbidden_behaviors: Adds accountability pressure to make the ceremony feel useful.
Keeps the review unchanged because weekly cadence is conventional.
